site.name: Mossad
site.title: Mossad: meeting notes and work intelligence for your Mac
site.description: Free, open source work intelligence for your Mac. Mossad turns your Zoom, Meet, and Teams calls into notes and transcripts, and keeps track of people and promises.

launchChecks: scripts/release.sh publishes Mossad-<version>.zip and appcast.xml, not a DMG. A stable link to a DMG needs a DMG with a fixed name in each release (for example Mossad.dmg at releases/latest/download/Mossad.dmg). Until then, the download button points to the latest release page.
project.yml signs with 'Apple Development', and release.sh does not notarize. A copy downloaded on another Mac needs a Developer ID signature and notarization to open without a Gatekeeper warning.
The iPhone app is not in the App Store. The copy below says to build it with Xcode.

headlines: Meeting notes that write themselves, on your Mac.
Take your calls. Mossad keeps the notes.
Every call, written down. No bot on the call.
hero.subhead: Mossad is a free, open source menu bar app for macOS. It notices your Zoom, Google Meet, and Microsoft Teams calls, records them on your Mac, and writes a Markdown note for each one: a summary, decisions, action items, and a transcript that knows who spoke.
hero.image: The meeting page: the lanes player with one lane per speaker, over the Summary tab.

howItWorks.title: How it works
howItWorks.intro: You take your calls as usual. There is nothing to start and nothing to stop.

steps.title: It notices the call
steps.body: Every two seconds, Mossad checks which app uses the microphone and whether a meeting window or tab is open. When both are true, it starts to record.

steps.title: It records two tracks on your Mac
steps.body: Your microphone is one track. The call app's audio is the other, taken from that app alone, so your music and notifications stay out. The call ends when its window or tab closes.

steps.title: It transcribes and knows the voices
steps.body: After the call, the provider you chose transcribes each track. Mossad joins them, removes the echo of the other side from your track, and matches each voice to the people you have named.

steps.title: It writes a Markdown note
steps.body: A model you chose writes the summary, decisions, and action items. Mossad saves one note per call in ~/Mossad/Meetings, ready for you and for your AI tools.

featureGroups.title: Capture
featureGroups.intro: Mossad records without a bot in the meeting and without a click from you.
featureGroups.image: The menu bar panel during a call: Recording, the platform, the time, Pause and Stop.

features.title: Finds your calls
features.body: Mossad starts to record when Zoom, Microsoft Teams, or a Meet or Teams tab in your browser is in a real meeting.
details: Zoom and Microsoft Teams apps
Google Meet and Teams in Chrome, Arc, Safari, Edge, and Brave
When an app seems to be in a call that Mossad cannot confirm, one notification offers Record

features.title: Stops when the call ends
features.body: The recording ends when the meeting window or tab closes, not after a guess from a few quiet seconds.
details: If that signal is missing, three minutes without microphone use end the call
Calls shorter than one minute are not kept

features.title: Two tracks, no bot
features.body: Your voice and the other side are recorded apart, so the transcript never confuses you with them.
details: The call track comes from a Core Audio tap on the call app only
Echo of the other side that your microphone picks up is removed from your track
Nobody joins your meeting and nothing appears in the call

features.title: Muted means silent
features.body: When you mute in the call app, Mossad writes silence over your track for that time.

features.title: Pause, stop, or skip
features.body: Pause a recording, stop it early, or skip a call and delete it from the menu bar.
details: Mark a meeting or a whole series in the calendar as do not record
Record a meeting in a room by hand

features.title: Your call comes first
features.body: Heavy work waits until the call ends, so the call keeps the processor and the network.
details: An update that you accept during a call installs after the call
Process now runs a waiting meeting at once

featureGroups.title: Notes and transcripts
featureGroups.intro: Each call becomes one plain Markdown file that you own.
featureGroups.image: A meeting page with the Summary tab: topics, decisions with their times, action items.

features.title: One note per call
features.body: Every call is a Markdown file with front matter, a summary, action items, decisions, and the transcript.
details: Named by date and title, so it sorts in Finder
Front matter with date, platform, attendees, speakers, kind, and tags
Readable by any editor and any AI agent

features.title: Summaries by topic
features.body: A short overview, one section per topic, decisions with the moment they were made, and action items with owners.
details: Long meetings are summarized in parts
Regenerate a summary at any time

features.title: Real meeting titles
features.body: A meeting takes its title from the calendar invite, or Mossad names it from what was said.
details: A first title shows about five minutes into the call
A title you type is never replaced

features.title: Live transcript
features.body: Read the call as it happens, with the voices that Mossad knows already named.
details: Optional; it uses AssemblyAI streaming
Off on a network in Low Data Mode

features.title: See who spoke when
features.body: The player shows one lane per speaker across the whole meeting; click a lane to hear that moment.
details: Decisions and bookmarks are marks on the timeline
Each speaker keeps one color in the lanes and the transcript

features.title: Nothing gets lost
features.body: Each step saves its result, so a sleep, a lost network, or a quit picks up where it stopped.
details: Failed steps try again with backoff
Transcribe a meeting again, with one undo

featureGroups.title: People and voices
featureGroups.intro: Name a voice once. Mossad knows it on every call after that.
featureGroups.image: A person's profile: meetings, talk time, who they meet with, and their action items.

features.title: Name a voice once
features.body: Each speaker gets a voice fingerprint on your Mac; name a new one and Mossad recognizes that person from then on.
details: One notification after a call with new voices, and nothing more
Play a short clip, then type a name or pick an invited person
Turn voice recognition off, or delete all saved voices, in Settings

features.title: Voices that read the invite
features.body: Mossad uses the call's invite to name voices: a person who was not invited needs a much closer match.
details: When one invited person has no saved voice and one voice is left, Mossad names it and learns it
A voice named from the invite names nobody on a call that does not invite that person, until a later call confirms it
Any of a person's addresses on the invite finds their voice
Calls with no invite keep the usual rules

features.title: A page for each person
features.body: See every meeting with a person, your talk time together, who they meet with, and their open action items.
details: Rename, merge, or delete a person
A review of likely duplicates
Sort by recent, most met, talk time, or name

features.title: Person pages with tabs
features.body: A person's page has tabs for the overview, meetings, tasks, analytics, knowledge, and voice, and every address they use finds them.
details: More than one email for each person, and "Not their address" for one that is wrong
Your company's domains and directory aliases count as theirs
Your points for the next time you see them, on the overview

features.title: Your org chart
features.body: Import an org chart from a CSV file, and People shows each person's title, manager, and team.
details: Titles give the summaries and the coach context

features.title: How to present to them
features.body: After a few calls, a card says how a person likes to hear things, with each point tied to what they said.
details: Shown only after three calls, or two with strong signs
The model sees handles such as P1, never names
Turn it off for any person

featureGroups.title: Coach
featureGroups.intro: A coach that reads your calls and gives you one thing to work on, with the proof.
featureGroups.image: The Findings deck on Coach: one card with a moment from a call and its Useful and Not useful answers.

features.body: After each call, the coach gives at most one piece of advice, and only with a moment or a number to back it.
details: Pace, filler words, turns, questions, and cut-ins from the transcript
Pitch, loudness, and trailing off from your own track
The same skill gets no new advice for 30 days

features.title: Findings you can answer
features.body: Swipe through short cards about your calls; each yes or no teaches the coach what helps you.
details: Each card says why it matters
Never again blocks a subject until you undo it
On the Mac and the iPhone

features.title: Goals with a number
features.body: Take on a goal such as more room in your 1:1s, and see it measured meeting by meeting.
details: Progress comes from your talk share, not from the model's opinion

features.title: A weekly review

Send through Resend, Postmark, SendGrid, Mailgun, Brevo, or Amazon SES

features.title: It remembers

features.title: Was it worth it

features.title: Before this meeting
features.body: Open an upcoming meeting to see who is coming, what happened last time, and what you still owe them.
details: When you last met each person, and how often
The last meeting's decisions and action items
Your open tasks for these people
Join from the same page

Add a point from Chat or from another AI app

features.title: A search in every list

Recent searches before you type
Bookmark notes and job titles in the results

details: Works while the call app is in front
All bookmarks of all meetings on one page

details: Off by default
Only the meeting window, and only the frames that change
Screen images never sync

features.title: What you promised

features.title: A calendar of your meetings

featureGroups.title: Analytics

featureGroups.image: The 'How you communicate' chart: talk share per meeting with the weekly line and the usual band.

features.body: Talk time, turns, cut-ins, questions, and silence for one meeting, each next to its usual value.

features.title: All on your Mac
features.body: Pick local transcription and a local or on-device model, and your audio and text never leave your Mac.
details: Voice recognition always runs on your Mac

features.title: Your keys, your bills

privacy.title: Private by design
privacy.intro: Mossad is local first. Your meetings stay in a folder on your Mac, and you decide where they go.

points.title: Local first
points.body: Notes, audio, voice fingerprints, and the coach's memory are files in ~/Mossad. There is no Mossad account, and no Mossad cloud holds your meetings.

points.title: Your keys
points.body: You bring your own provider keys. They live only in your Mac's Keychain, and each provider bills you directly.

points.title: Your server
points.body: Sync, share links, the remote MCP, and backups run on a server in your own Cloudflare account, or not at all.

points.title: Your words stay yours
points.body: Your meetings, recordings, names, and words stay on your Mac, except where you send them: to the providers, servers, and devices that you choose.

leavesTheMac.title: Where your meetings can go
items: Audio, to the transcription provider you chose. Nothing, if you transcribe on your Mac.
Live audio while you record, to AssemblyAI, if the live transcript is on.
Transcript text, to the AI provider you chose for notes, chat, and the coach. Nothing, with a local or on-device model.
Meetings, to your iPhone through iCloud or through your own server, if you turn on sync.
Recordings, to Cloudflare R2, Amazon S3, or your own server, if you turn on backup.
One meeting, to your own server, when you share it.
Read-only requests to Google, if you connect Google.
The weekly review, to your own email address through your mail provider, if you turn it on.
A check for updates to GitHub.
leavesTheMac.neverLeaves: Voice fingerprints never leave your Mac. Shared-screen images never sync.

openSource.title: Free and open source
openSource.body: Mossad is free and released under the MIT License. Read every line, build it yourself, change it, or send a fix.
points: The Mac app, the iPhone app, and the server are in one repository
More than 2,000 unit tests run without a network
Design documents for each part are in docs/

faq.question: What does Mossad cost?
faq.answer: Mossad is free. The cloud providers that you connect bill you directly: cloud transcription is about $0.22 to $0.36 an hour of audio, and the notes model adds its own cost. Setup shows the cost per hour of your choices, and the Analytics page shows what each meeting cost. With local models, it costs nothing.

faq.question: Where do my recordings and notes go?
faq.answer: Into ~/Mossad on your Mac. Audio goes to the transcription provider you chose, and the transcript goes to the AI provider you chose, unless you choose models that run on your Mac. Your meetings, recordings, and names go nowhere else unless you turn on sync, backup, sharing, Google, or the weekly email.

faq.question: Do I have to tell people that I record?
faq.answer: Yes. Mossad does not announce itself on the call, so telling people is your job. Many places require the consent of one or of all people on a call, and voice fingerprints can be biometric data under some laws. Read the Lawful use section of the README, and ask a lawyer if you are not sure.

faq.question: Which call apps does it work with?
faq.answer: Zoom, Microsoft Teams, and Google Meet. It reads meeting tabs in Chrome, Arc, Safari, Edge, and Brave. In a browser whose tabs it cannot read, such as Firefox, it tells you once and offers to record. You can also record a meeting in a room by hand.

faq.question: Does a bot join my meeting?
faq.answer: No. Mossad records on your Mac from your microphone and the call app's audio. Nothing joins the call and nothing shows to the other people.

faq.question: Can it run without the cloud?
faq.answer: Yes. Choose a transcription model that runs on your Mac (Parakeet, Whisper, Apple Speech, or Qwen3-ASR) and a local server such as Ollama or LM Studio, or Apple's on-device model, for the notes. Then audio and text stay on your Mac. Local models are free; quality and speed depend on the model and your Mac.

faq.question: Is there an iPhone app?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows your meetings, chat, people, analytics, and the coach, and it records meetings in a room for your Mac to write up. It syncs through iCloud or your own server. It is not in the App Store; build it from the source with Xcode.

faq.question: How do updates work?
faq.answer: Mossad checks the latest GitHub release and offers each new version. It installs an update only when its signature matches the key built into the app, and an update that you accept during a call waits until the call ends. Settings lets you turn automatic checks and installs on or off.

faq.question: Do I need my own server?
faq.answer: No. Mossad works on your Mac alone, and iCloud syncs your iPhone. The server is for share links, the remote MCP for web AI apps, sync without iCloud, and recording backup. It runs on Cloudflare's free plan for one person.

faq.question: Can other AI apps read my meetings?
faq.answer: Yes, if you want. Run Mossad --mcp to give Claude Desktop, Claude Code, or any MCP client read access on your Mac. With your own server, ChatGPT and Claude on the web can connect after you sign in. The notes are also plain Markdown files that any agent can read.

faq.question: What if Mossad gets a name or a summary wrong?
faq.answer: Rename a voice and every note updates. Edit a title, regenerate a summary, or transcribe a meeting again. Summaries, coaching, and person notes come from software and can be wrong, so check them before you act on them.

footer.text: Mossad is free and open source under the MIT License. It is provided as is, without warranty of any kind, and it gives no legal or professional advice. Use it only in a lawful way: tell the people you record, get consent where the law requires it, and follow the privacy laws and the rules of your organization. Zoom, Google Meet, Gemini, Microsoft Teams, and other names belong to their owners; Mossad is not affiliated with them.
